title: Adobe releases Lightroom Classic 16.0 and Lightroom 10.0: Glow, Vectorscope, AI depth masks and tethering on Lightroom desktop
summary: Adobe releases Lightroom Classic 16.0 and Lightroom 10.0: Glow, Vectorscope, AI depth masks and tethering…
detailed: Adobe has released Lightroom Classic 16.0, Lightroom 10.0 (desktop) and Lightroom Mobile 12.0 to coincide with Adobe MAX 2026.

Highlights include a new Glow effect (Bloom, Halation, Diffusion, Motion and Streak), a Vectorscope, AI-generated depth maps for masking, Color Grading inside masks, AI blemish removal, an autofocus point overlay in Classic, and tethered shooting in Lightroom desktop and on iPad for the first time.
Glow is available in Classic, Lightroom desktop, and Lightroom on iPhone, iPad and Android.
For more information, see Adobe’s Lightroom desktop release notes , the Lightroom desktop what’s new page and the Lightroom Classic release notes .
sentences: Adobe has released Lightroom Classic 16.0, Lightroom 10.0 (desktop) and Lightroom Mobile 12.0 to coincide with Adobe MAX 2026.
This is the annual major-version update, and it is a big one.

Highlights include a new Glow effect (Bloom, Halation, Diffusion, Motion and Streak), a Vectorscope, AI-generated depth maps for masking, Color Grading inside masks, AI blemish removal, an autofocus point overlay in Classic, and tethered shooting in Lightroom desktop and on iPad for the first time.
Several of these tools have lived in Adobe Camera Raw for some time.
Lightroom Classic 16.0 ships with Camera Raw 19.0.
Glow adds diffusion-filter and film-style light effects in post.
There are five styles: Bloom, Diffusion, Halation, Motion and Streak.
Motion and Streak add Direction and Softness sliders.
Style, Range, Spread and Warmth are shared between the global adjustment and every mask, so only the Glow amount can be set per mask.
You cannot combine different Glow styles in one image using separate masks.
Lightroom Classic also gets Glow presets: Sheer, Dream, Soft Bloom, Strong Bloom, Gentle Aura and Cinematic Glow.
Glow is available in Classic, Lightroom desktop, and Lightroom on iPhone, iPad and Android.
Anyone who grades video will recognize this one.
The Vectorscope plots color on a wheel, with hue as position around the circle and saturation as distance from the center.
Adobe includes a skin-tone line for checking faces.
Hovering over the image shows crosshairs with that pixel’s color and RGB values, and with a mask selected the scope shows only the masked pixels.
In Classic, the Vectorscope lives in the Histogram panel (right-click the Histogram) and can preview in Adobe RGB or sRGB.
In Lightroom desktop it is accessed from the right Toolstrip.
AI blemish removal detects and removes skin blemishes, moles and freckles using Content-Aware Remove.
There are separate sliders for Blemishes (temporary marks) and Natural Marks (moles and freckles), plus Remove and Restore brushes for refinement.
Individual faces in group photos can be adjusted separately.
In Lightroom desktop, a Refine brush and Fade control fine-tune the result.
It is available across Classic, desktop and mobile.
Open Eyes, labeled Early Access, uses AI to correct closed or partly closed eyes, using other photos of the same person as a reference.
It is in Lightroom desktop and in Quick Actions on mobile.
It uses Generative Credits and saves the result as a new DNG.
Lightroom desktop and Lightroom for iPad now support tethered capture for Canon, Nikon, Sony and Fujifilm cameras.
Features include Live View, overlays, multiple connected cameras, and automatic application of presets and keywords as images come in.
Tethering also works in Local mode, and diagnostic logs help troubleshoot connection issues.
Adobe says desktop supports the same cameras as Classic, plus camera setting controls that Classic lacks.
Lightroom Classic 16.0 adds official tether support for a number of older Canon, Leica and Sony bodies.
Adobe has not published a model list in the release notes.
Camera support is limited this round: the Apple iPhone Duo Ultrawide and Wide cameras.
12-month Creative Cloud Photography Plan subscriptions are also available from B&H .
For more information, see Adobe’s Lightroom desktop release notes , the Lightroom desktop what’s new page and the Lightroom Classic release notes .
